title: Google Tag Manager (GTM) Client & Server-Side Architecture
overview: Google Tag Manager orchestrates tag deployment, consent mode signals, and server-side event routing without requiring frequent frontend code modifications.
coreConcepts: dataLayer structured JavaScript object storing interaction parameters
Triggers based on pageview, custom events, element visibility, and form submissions
Variables for dynamic data retrieval (URL query parameters, JS variables, DOM elements)
Server-Side GTM container running on isolated Cloud Run / Docker proxy
features: Google Tag (gtag.js) unified configuration entity across GA4 and Google Ads
Built-in Consent Mode v2 integration with Consent Management Platforms (CMPs)
Preview Mode with real-time tag firing diagnostics and variable inspection
Version control with rollback history and environment staging
bestPractices: Maintain strict single dataLayer.push() schema across development sprints
Never hardcode personal user data in the client-side dataLayer
Migrate high-volume conversion tags to Server-Side GTM for page speed and adblocker mitigation
Always run preview mode tests across mobile and desktop breakpoints before publishing
policies: Tag firing must respect user consent choices declared via CMP
Prohibition of keylogger scripts or unauthorized third-party tracking injections
Content Security Policy (CSP) compliant script hash generation
limitations: Client-side GTM script execution subject to client adblockers and Brave Shields
Maximum container size limit: 200 KB per published container
Server-side container requires cloud infrastructure hosting costs
commonIssues: Tags firing multiple times per pageview due to duplicate triggers
dataLayer values undefined when tags trigger before the dataLayer push finishes
Ad blocker preventing GTM bootstrap script (gtm.js) from loading

troubleshootingGuide.issue: Tag fires before dataLayer variables are populated
troubleshootingGuide.resolution: Change trigger from 'Page View' to 'Custom Event' that fires immediately following the dataLayer push
Deploy Server-Side GTM with custom first-party subdomain mapping (e.g. data.clientdomain.com)
